issues.description: raise PerformanceWarning conflates warning and error contracts
issues.detail: PerformanceWarning is a Warning subclass meant for warnings.warn(), but the code raises it as a hard exception. This breaks the implicit contract that warnings are advisory and leaves callers unable to reason about whether this is a soft signal or hard stop. Either use warnings.warn() or raise a proper ValueError/RuntimeError. The test enshrines the mistake via pytest.raises(PerformanceWarning).

issues.description: unreachable break after raise reveals undecided control-flow intent
issues.detail: The `break` immediately following `raise PerformanceWarning(msg)` is dead code. It signals the author was torn between fail-fast on first misalignment versus aggregate-and-report all axes. Pick one posture, document it, and delete the other. Dead code in a validation path is a tell that the contract was never specified.

issues.description: policy decision belongs in a dedicated helper, not inline in to_zarr
issues.detail: The 20-line validation block embeds global-config-vs-shard-shape policy inside to_zarr's write mechanism. Extract a pure `validate_shard_alignment(zarr_chunks, dask_chunks, dtype) -> Optional[str]` (or `_resolve_write_chunks`) helper. Data in, message out, no state. to_zarr then decides what to do with the result — separating mechanism from policy.

issues.description: safe_chunk_size uses suspicious max(1, itemsize) guard that hides intent
issues.detail: `np.prod(zarr_write_chunks) * max(1, z.dtype.itemsize)` papers over a real question: numpy itemsize is always >= 1 for real dtypes. Either the guard is dead (delete it) or it silently handles object/structured dtypes that deserve explicit handling. The error message also leaks an internal computation as a recommended user-facing config value.

issues.description: PR's core design question (config vs shard shape ownership) left unresolved
issues.detail: Three stories disagree: the docstring says "performance warning," the message says "to avoid risk of data loss," the code raises. The PR description itself asks who owns chunking policy when global `array.chunk-size` config and zarr shard shape compete. Decide ownership (zarr-shard-wins, config-wins-with-error, explicit-override-required) and make code, tests, and message tell the same story.

issues.description: per-axis check inspects only dw[0] and reads backwards
issues.detail: `normalize_chunks` returns per-block tuples that need not be uniform; checking `dw[0] % zw` assumes uniformity and silently passes if interior blocks differ. Additionally `not nominal_dask_chunk_size % zw == 0` relies on fragile precedence — write `% zw != 0` for obvious intent. State the invariant on the full value, not its first element.

synthesis.summary: The panel reaches strong consensus that the core defect is a confused contract: `raise PerformanceWarning(msg)` conflates warning and error semantics, with an unreachable `break` after it betraying that the author never decided between warn-and-continue and fail-fast. All three reviewers want the inline 20-line validation block extracted into a pure helper that separates alignment policy from to_zarr's write mechanism. Secondary issues include a suspicious `max(1, itemsize)` guard, a per-axis check that only inspects the first chunk, and backwards-reading boolean precedence. Above all, the PR's own open question — who owns chunking when global config and shard shape compete — must be decided before merge so code, docstring, message, and tests tell one story.
